bullets.text: Machine Learning (ML) is a fast-growing area in technology.
ML is a subfield of Artificial Intelligence (AI), focused on systems learning from data.
Models learn patterns from data to make decisions or predictions, rather than being explicitly programmed.
ML models improve over time with more data without needing reprogramming.
Machine learning is ubiquitous, powering recommendation systems, spam filters, and virtual assistants.
Its popularity stems from access to vast amounts of data.
Increased computational power (GPUs) enables efficient data processing.
Development of sophisticated algorithms extracts better insights from data.
One of three main types of ML, and the most common in industry.
Models are trained using labeled data, where each input has a correct output.
Goal is to predict outputs for new, unseen inputs based on learned relationships.
Example: predicting house prices based on features and past sale prices.
Categories include regression (continuous values) and classification (discrete labels like spam/not spam).
Uses unlabeled data, meaning only inputs are provided without explicit answers.
Algorithms discover patterns, relationships, or structures independently.
Common application is clustering, e.g., grouping customers by buying behavior.
Also used for dimensionality reduction to simplify data with many features.
An agent learns by interacting with an environment.
Decisions lead to feedback (rewards or penalties), adjusting the agent's strategy.
Goal is to learn a policy that maximizes total reward over time.
Examples include training robots to walk or AI to play games like chess (AlphaGo).
Applied in robotics, game-playing AI, finance, and self-driving cars.
Data quality is crucial; noisy, biased, or incomplete data harms model performance.
Overfitting occurs when a model learns training data too well but fails on new data.
Ethical concerns arise from biased data leading to biased models with real-world consequences.
ML requires understanding data, context, and the impact of models, not just algorithms.
Recap of ML definition, importance, three types, and challenges.
Future lectures will delve deeper into each ML type, algorithms, and practical examples.
